editorial:
Ray Breslin is the best in the business at breaking out of prisons, so when he gets locked inside a secret high-tech facility he helped design, the stakes could not be higher. Sylvester Stallone plays Ray with his usual tough-guy charm, while Arnold Schwarzenegger steals scenes as Rottmayer, a fellow inmate who becomes his unlikely partner. The movie has a fun, old-school action vibe that feels like a throwback to the 1980s, with plenty of fistfights, clever escape tricks, and a creepy warden played by Jim Caviezel. The prison itself looks cold and high-tech, and watching Ray figure out its weaknesses is genuinely entertaining.

The action is solid and the pacing keeps you moving, though the plot can feel a bit predictable and some dialogue is cheesy. Still, seeing Stallone and Schwarzenegger team up is worth the price of admission alone. If you enjoy classic action movies with big stars and simple thrills, this one delivers. endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ray and Rottmayer stage a massive prison riot that lets them reach the helicopter pad. Warden Hobbes tries to stop them but is killed during the chaos, and Ray escapes by helicopter with help from his team back home. The twist is that Rottmayer was not just a random inmate—he was a former CIA operative imprisoned for knowing too much, and Ray's partners had been tracking him the whole time. Ray returns to his firm, and the conspiracy behind his framing is exposed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic action movies with big stars and simple thrills.
